author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Boston police arrested a 35-year-old Dorchester woman after a stabbing near 950 Blue Hill Avenue on Thursday evening. Authorities identified the suspect as Jasmine Noiles and said she faces assault and battery charges, including assault and battery causing serious bodily injury.

The Boston Police Department said officers responded to the Blue Hill Avenue area and made the arrest in connection with the reported stabbing. NBC10 Boston reported the case Friday as detectives continued reviewing the circumstances. Officials had not released the injured person's name or a detailed account of what led to the encounter in the initial public notice.

Noiles is expected to be arraigned in Boston Municipal Court, where prosecutors will present the allegations and a judge will determine release conditions. The charges are accusations, and she is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police did not immediately disclose whether the people involved knew one another or provide an updated condition for the injured person. Anyone with information can contact Boston police; anonymous tips may be submitted through the department's CrimeStoppers program.
dek: Boston police arrested Jasmine Noiles, 35, after a Thursday-evening stabbing near 950 Blue Hill Avenue.
headline: Dorchester woman charged after Blue Hill Avenue stabbing
